description: Adds cluster_affinity and target_customer_origin fields to each business family. These fields are additive — they do not replace any existing field. Merge by matching on 'id'.

governance_rules.affinity_note: synergistic means co-location increases mutual demand (agglomeration effect). competitive means co-location may cannibalize demand. neutral means no meaningful interaction expected.

target_customer_origin.purpose: Declares where the primary customer base comes from. Drives which tract indicators are most relevant: resident → income/demographics; daytime_worker → LEHD office worker concentration; destination_visitor → regional draw, premium cluster; passing_traffic → transit/footfall/road counts.
target_customer_origin.scoring_implication: The fit score should weight tract indicators proportionally to this origin mix. A business with 0.8 daytime_worker weight should care far more about office_worker_presence than about median_age of residents.

structure.synergistic: list of business_family_ids — co-location increases mutual demand
structure.competitive: list of business_family_ids — co-location may reduce demand or margin
structure.neutral: list of business_family_ids — no meaningful interaction expected

cluster_affinity.purpose: Enables category-aware density scoring. A tract's commercial density should be weighted by the affinity composition of that density, not treated as a flat count.
cluster_affinity.scoring_implication: compatible_business_cluster indicator = weighted sum of nearby businesses by affinity value (synergistic: +1.0, neutral: 0.0, competitive: -0.5). This replaces raw business_density for cluster-sensitive business types.

cluster_affinity_notes: Retail storefronts benefit from being in active mixed-use strips where complementary services draw dwell time.
Competition from identical retail type is real but manageable if product differentiation is strong.
In a luxury positioning scenario, competitive becomes synergistic — see luxury_cluster_fit need.
Sit-down restaurants benefit strongly from daytime worker lunch demand.
Restaurant rows show agglomeration: competing restaurants often increase the area's collective draw.
Evening positioning shifts weight toward destination_visitor and nightlife synergy.
Quick service is the most daytime_worker-dependent family in the entire taxonomy.
Proximity to office clusters is the single strongest location signal for this type.
Transit stops amplify passing_traffic significantly for this format.
Nightlife is one of the strongest agglomeration-positive categories: competing venues increase the district's gravitational pull.
After-work transition from daytime_worker to destination_visitor is a key demand pattern.
Child-sensitive and medical uses nearby are risk signals, not synergies.
Professional services cluster is strongly self-reinforcing: lawyers near accountants near consultants create referral ecosystems.
Being in an established professional cluster signals legitimacy to clients.
Note: competitive list is empty — competing firms often increase the area's credibility rather than cannibalizing it.
Medical uses agglomerate strongly — patients bundle errands when visiting healthcare districts.
A pediatric practice has very different resident demographics requirements than a geriatric practice: age-band matching is critical and not captured by median_age alone.
Specialist practices have larger destination_visitor radius than GPs.
Repeat neighborhood clientele is the dominant pattern — proximity to dense residential is more important than premium location.
At the luxury end (high-end salon), the model shifts: destination_visitor weight rises, luxury_cluster_fit need activates.
Competition is real at commodity price points; differentiation (specialty, premium) reduces it.
Morning and evening peaks mean daytime_worker and resident weights are nearly equal.
Boutique fitness (yoga, pilates, barre) shows strong agglomeration with health-adjacent retail and cafes — the 'wellness strip' pattern.
Large parking_need reflects suburban membership model; transit-accessible urban studios shift the weight toward daytime_worker.
Child-oriented services depend strongly on family_proxy and the 25-44 age band of parents — median_age is insufficient.
Drop-off/pick-up traffic patterns create very specific parking and road access needs.
Adult training (language school, coding academy) shifts target_customer_origin toward daytime_worker significantly.
These are back-office operations. The 'customer' is often another business, not a resident.
Vehicle logistics and yard space matter more than any demographic signal.
Clustering with other service businesses creates convenience for shared suppliers.
Maker/artisan clusters are self-reinforcing: a district known for craft attracts buyers and collaborators alike.
B2B and B2C mixed: destination_visitor comes to buy; daytime_worker comes to collaborate or supply.
Gentrification signal: maker clusters often precede premium retail by 3-7 years in urban transitions.
Almost entirely B2B. Resident demographics are nearly irrelevant.
Road network quality and truck access are the dominant location signals.
Clustered logistics zones reduce per-unit infrastructure cost — agglomeration is economically rational.
Hybrid concepts are most sensitive to the mix of the immediate street — they need complementary activity, not just density.
classification_ambiguity is high: the dominant activity (retail vs. service) determines which origin weights apply.
A florist-with-workshop leans destination_visitor; a bike-repair-and-sales leans resident.
Creative clusters are the strongest agglomeration-positive category after nightlife and professional services.
Talent attraction is the primary location logic, not customer footfall.
Transit access matters more than parking: knowledge workers skew toward walkable, transit-served urban cores.
Proximity to cafes and restaurants is a soft retention signal ('amenity richness').
Cannot be assigned until the concept is decomposed into its dominant operational behaviors.
Default origin weights are a placeholder — they should be overwritten after clarification.
This family should trigger the clarification_question flow before any scoring is attempted.
